_provenance: PLAN A-15 (TSPEC §11.2, D-6). This file is an AUTHORED, hand-reviewed literal —
never computed by the system under test (the whole point of D-6). It was
produced ONCE by instrumenting orchestrate-dev.js's `_writeFile` / `_appendFile`
/ `_git` seams for a full pipeline run at the pre-feature baseline commit
26c3f1c, in a detached, throwaway `git worktree add --detach` scratch
directory OUTSIDE this repo tree (never `git checkout` — the orchestrator
owns the branch and TSPEC §2.3 forbids it), then removed with
`git worktree remove`. The exact capture invocation is recorded in
`scenario.command` below.
What 'created file' means for this baseline, given what the three
instrumented seams actually see at 26c3f1c:
- `_writeFile` is a declared seam with ZERO call sites in orchestrate-dev.js
at this commit — it is dead code at this baseline, so it contributes no
paths.
- REQ/FSPEC/TSPEC/PLAN/PROPERTIES/DECISIONS/LEARNINGS/CODE_REVIEW document
CONTENT is authored by the dispatched author/reviewer/dod-verify/harvest
agents themselves, through their own tool use — entirely outside these
three script-owned seams. A disabled-tier run therefore observes none of
that content creation through instrumentation; only the pipeline's own
mechanical bookkeeping shows up below.
- `_appendFile` fires once per approving cross-review round (§5.3 t5): the
APPROVAL-HASH / REVIEWED-COMMIT anchor pair appended to each of the two
reviewers' cross-review files, for every phase whose reviewLoop converges
(R, F, T, P, PR — D is skipped in this scenario, so it contributes none).
- `_git` fires for the branch guard's read-only `rev-parse` checks (not
creations), for the `git add` + `git commit` pair that follows each
successful anchor append (§5.3 t6), and for the wave-mode gate's
`commitPaths` call that stages and commits each Phase I task's own
owned files per the PLAN's file-ownership manifest.
- Phase MERGE contributes nothing: `mergeMode` resolves to its documented
default `off` when `.claude/pdlc.config.json` is absent, so the phase
resolves `skipped` before any `_git` call.
Regenerating this fixture is a deliberate act (TSPEC §11.2): re-state the
`scenario` object below in full — a stale scenario fails the D-6 comparison
as fixture staleness, not as a created-file diff.
